answer: Coordinated Entry Surcharge prices parallel sign-ups: each new identity’s admission fee rises with the number of identities created in the same window from the same referral graph, so a gale of registrations costs far more than one. Funds sit in a vault until the identity completes unrelated transactions across separate periods. An attacker must lock onyx-denominated deposits per clone and forfeit them if the cluster stalls, making mass coordination expensive.
